column2: Come, I shall tell you what I asked of my teacher long ago, Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa, the great sage who arranged the Veda.
Sumantu, Jaimini, Paila of firm vows, I as the fourth pupil, and Shuka remembered as the fifth.
These five pupils gathered, self-controlled, joined with purity and good conduct, with anger conquered and senses mastered,
he taught the Vedas, with the Mahabharata as the fifth, on Meru, the best of mountains, lovely and frequented by Siddhas and Charanas.
As they were studying the Vedas, a doubt once arose among them; this is what you have now asked, and it was explained to them; I heard it then too, and must tell it to you today, Bharata.
Hearing the pupils' words, the glorious Vyasa, Parashara's son, remover of the darkness of all ignorance, spoke.

I have practised a very great and most severe austerity, good ones, that I might know past, present and future.
mahabharata:12:327.22	By Narayana's grace, for me of practised austerity and restrained senses, beside the Milk Ocean,
mahabharata:12:327.23	this threefold-time knowledge appeared as I wished. Hear it; as the knowledge is, I shall tell the excellent doubt, as it happened at the beginning of the age, seen by my eye of knowledge.
mahabharata:12:327.24	Him whom those who know Sankhya and yoga call the Supreme Self gets the name Great Person by his own deed.
mahabharata:12:327.25	From him was born the unmanifest, which the wise know as Pradhana; from the unmanifest the manifest arose, from the lord, for the creation of the worlds.
mahabharata:12:327.26	Aniruddha is called in the worlds the Great Self; he who has reached manifestation and made the grandfather is called ego, for he is made wholly of splendour.
mahabharata:12:327.27	Earth, wind, space, water, and light as the fifth: these great elements, Bharata, are born of ego.
mahabharata:12:327.28	Having created the great elements, he again made their qualities; hear of the embodied ones made from the elements.
mahabharata:12:327.29	Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, the great-souled Vasishtha, and Manu Svayambhuva: these are to be known as the eight natures in which the worlds are established.
mahabharata:12:327.30	Brahma, grandfather of the worlds, made the Vedas with their limbs and sacrifices with their parts for the success of the worlds; from the eight natures this universe was born.
mahabharata:12:327.31	Rudra, of the nature of wrath, was born and himself created ten others; these eleven Rudras are remembered as modifications, persons.
mahabharata:12:327.32	Those Rudras and the nature, and all the divine sages, born for the success of the worlds, approached Brahma.
mahabharata:12:327.33	We have been created by you, blessed one, the mighty; in what office each of us is to act, grandfather,
the office you have assigned, thinking of its purpose: how is that office to be kept by the holder of the office?
Give strength to him who is concerned with the purpose of the office." Thus addressed, Mahadeva spoke to those gods:

Well have I been informed by you, gods; blessings on you; this concern which you have is arisen in me also.
mahabharata:12:327.37	How is the whole system of the world to be taken up, and how may no loss of strength befall you and me?
mahabharata:12:327.38	From here let us all go for refuge to the witness of the worlds, the Great Person, the unmanifest; he will tell us what is beneficial.
Then those sages and gods, with Brahma, wishing the good of the worlds, went to the northern bank of the Milk Ocean.
They took up austerity, ordained by the Veda and spoken by Brahma, a most severe austerity named the Great Observance.
With eyes and arms upward, with minds one-pointed, standing on one foot, rightly composed like logs,
for a divine thousand years they practised that excellent austerity, and heard a sweet voice adorned with the Veda and its limbs:

Ho, gods with Brahma, and sages rich in austerity, honouring you all with a welcome, I tell you an excellent word.
mahabharata:12:327.44	I know your task, and that great one for the good of the world: a work of action, to be done, strengthening your lives.
mahabharata:12:327.45	Your austerity is well practised, gods, done from desire to please me; you, of great strength, will enjoy the excellent fruit of this austerity.
mahabharata:12:327.46	This is Brahma, teacher of the world, grandfather of all worlds; and you, best of the gods, worship me, composed.
mahabharata:12:327.47	Make portions for me always at sacrifices; and I shall ordain the good, lords, according to each one's office.
Hearing this word of the god of gods, with hair standing on end for joy, all those gods and Brahma and the great sages
performed a Vaishnava sacrifice by the rule seen in the Veda; at that sacrificial session Brahma himself made a share, and the gods and divine sages made shares.
The shares, highly honoured, with the duties of the task and the age, reached that Person of sun-colour beyond darkness, vast, all-pervading, the god, ruler, boon-giving lord.
Then the boon-giving god, to all those immortals standing there, bodiless, shone and spoke this word, standing in the sky, the great lord.

By whomever the share was made, it has come so; pleased, I give today the fruit marked by return.
mahabharata:12:327.53	This is your mark, gods, born of my grace: worshipped by you with sacrifices completed with full fees, age after age you will be enjoyers of the fruit of action.
mahabharata:12:327.54	And those men who in all the worlds sacrifice with sacrifices will make portions for you, gods, as ordained by the Veda.
mahabharata:12:327.55	Whoever has made a portion for me in this great sacrifice as arranged, he is made by me worthy of a share of the sacrifice in the Vedic aphorism.
mahabharata:12:327.56	You, risen by the fruit of the share of the sacrifice, support the worlds, thinking of every purpose in the world, formed according to your offices.
mahabharata:12:327.57	By those rites that will be performed, honoured by the fruit of action, with strength increased, you will support the worlds.
mahabharata:12:327.58	You are cherished in the world by men in all sacrifices; then you will cherish me; this is my cherishing of you.
mahabharata:12:327.59	For this purpose the Vedas and the sacrifices with herbs were created; when rightly employed, the gods on earth are pleased by these.
mahabharata:12:327.60	This making of yours, set by the quality of action, has been made by me, best of gods, until the end of the age; think, lords, of the good of the world according to your offices.
mahabharata:12:327.61	Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasishtha: these seven were made mind-born.
mahabharata:12:327.62	These were made chief knowers of the Veda and teachers of the Veda, and also upholders of the dharma of action, made under Prajapati.
mahabharata:12:327.63	This is the eternal path of those who act, manifested, called Aniruddha, the lord who creates the worlds.
mahabharata:12:327.64	Sana, Sanatsujata, Sanaka with Sanandana, Sanatkumara, Kapila, and the seventh Sanatana:
mahabharata:12:327.65	these seven are called the mind-born sages, sons of Brahma, with knowledge come of itself, standing in the dharma of withdrawal.
mahabharata:12:327.66	These are the chief knowers of yoga and of the dharma of Sankhya, teachers in the treatise of liberation and promoters of the dharma of liberation.
mahabharata:12:327.67	From the unmanifest, threefold in quality and great, from which I came forth before, that which is higher, conceived as the knower of the field, that am I, the path of those who act, hard to find for return.
mahabharata:12:327.68	However a creature is made, and in whatever action, in action or withdrawal, he helplessly enjoys its fruit.
mahabharata:12:327.69	This is Brahma, teacher of the world, lord, maker of the beginning of the world; he is your mother and father and grandfather. Instructed by me he will be the giver of boons to all beings.
mahabharata:12:327.70	And his younger brother Rudra, who arose from his forehead, instructed by Brahma, will be a giver of boons everywhere.
mahabharata:12:327.71	Go to your offices and think of them as ordained; let all rites go forward in all worlds without delay.
mahabharata:12:327.72	And let the deeds of beings and their goals be shown, and their lives with ages fixed, best of gods.
mahabharata:12:327.73	This is the Krita age, the best time, now going on; in this age sacrificial animals are not to be killed, not otherwise; here, gods, dharma will be fourfooted and whole.
mahabharata:12:327.74	Then the Treta age, in which the threefold Veda will be, in which animals sprinkled will be put to death at the sacrifice; there dharma will lack a fourth part.
mahabharata:12:327.75	Then the Dvapara age, a mixed time, and in that age dharma will lack two parts.
mahabharata:12:327.76	Then when Tishya comes, the age headed by Kali, dharma will stand on one foot only where it is.
[The gods said:] "When dharma stands on one foot, going anywhere, what are we to do, blessed one? Tell us that."

[The Blessed One said:] "Where the Vedas and sacrifices, austerity, truth, self-control and non-violence joined with dharma are practised, best of gods, that country is to be resorted to; let adharma not touch you with its foot."
[Vyasa said:] Thus instructed by the blessed one, the gods and troops of sages bowed to the blessed one and went to the countries they wished.
When the dwellers of heaven had gone, Brahma alone remained, wishing to see the blessed one established in the body of Aniruddha.
The god showed himself to him, taking the great form of Hayashiras, reciting the Vedas with their limbs, bearing a water-pot and a rosary.
Then seeing that god of boundless might with a horse's head, Brahma, lord and maker of the worlds, wishing the good of the worlds,
bowing his head to the boon-giver, praised him standing in front with joined palms; and embraced by the god, he was made to hear this speech:

Think rightly of all the courses of the world's work; you are the creator of all beings, you are lord and teacher of the world; with the burden placed on you I shall soon gain steadiness.
mahabharata:12:327.85	And when the gods' work becomes too hard for you, I shall come into manifestation, as a teacher of knowledge of the self.
Having said this, Hayashiras vanished right there, and Brahma, instructed by him, soon went to his own world.
Thus this greatly fortunate lotus-naveled eternal one is said to be the first taker at sacrifices and ever the upholder of sacrifice.
Standing in the dharma of withdrawal, the goal of those with imperishable dharma, he ordains the dharmas of action, making the world variegated.

He is the beginning, middle and end of creatures; he is creator, the thing created, doer and deed; asleep at the end of the age, having drawn in the worlds, awakened at the start of the age, he sent forth the world.
Bow to that god, without qualities and of the nature of qualities, unborn, of universal form, the abode of all the dwellers of heaven,
lord of the great elements, lord of the Rudras, lord of the Adityas, lord of the Vasus,
lord of the Ashvins, lord of the Maruts, lord of the Vedas and sacrifices, lord of the Vedangas,
Hari who ever dwells in the ocean, with hair of munja grass, peace of all beings, proclaimer of the dharma of liberation,
lord of austerities and splendours and of fame, lord of speech always, lord of rivers,
the matted-haired, the boar, the one-horned, the wise, Vivasvan, Hayashiras, ever bearing the fourfold form,
secret, to be seen by knowledge, imperishable and perishable; this god goes about, moving everywhere, unchanging.
Thus was this seen long ago by me with the eye of knowledge, and it has been told to you all in truth when I was asked.
Do my word, pupils: serve Hari the lord, sing him with Vedic words and worship him by rule."
[Vaishampayana said:] Thus told by the wise Veda Vyasa, we all, the pupils, and his son Shuka, knower of supreme dharma,
One becomes free of disease, radiant, endowed with strength and beauty; the afflicted is freed from disease, the bound from bondage.
One desiring a desire gains it and obtains long life; a brahmana would be a knower of all the Vedas, a kshatriya victorious, a vaishya of great gain, and a shudra would gain happiness.
The childless gains a son, a maiden the husband she wishes, a woman with a clinging embryo is freed, a pregnant woman bears a son, a barren woman gains offspring rich in sons and grandsons.
One who reads this on the road goes the road in safety; whatever desire one desires, one surely gains it.
This is the settled word of the great sage, the praise of the great-souled best of persons; hearing this assembly of sages and gods, devotees gain great happiness.
[Janamejaya said:] You ought to tell, for one eager to hear of Hari, lord of the lords of creatures, that hearing it I may be purified, like the spotless autumn moon.
[Vaishampayana said:] Hear, king, as Hari the all-pervading, with a pleased heart, told Phalguna the derivation of his own names, born of qualities and deeds.
By the names of that great-souled Keshava being recited, king, Phalguna, hero, asked Keshava:
[Arjuna said:] Blessed one, lord of past and future, imperishable creator of all beings, abode of the worlds, lord of the world, giver of fearlessness to the worlds,
those names of yours, god, sung by the great sages in the Vedas with the Puranas, which are secret by their deeds,
their derivation I wish to hear from you, Keshava; no other than you can tell the derivation of the names, lord.
[The Blessed One said:] In the Rig Veda, Yajur Veda, Atharva and Sama, in the Puranas with the Upanishads, and in astrology, Arjuna,
in Sankhya and in the treatise of yoga and in Ayurveda, many names of mine have been sung by the great sages.
By whose grace Brahma was born, and Rudra born of anger, who is the womb of all, moving and unmoving,
that sattva of eighteen qualities, best of the good, that supreme nature, for me upholder of yoga, heaven and earth, the truth, the true, unconquerable by the gods, called the self of the worlds.
From that proceed all the changes of creation and dissolution; from it sacrifice, the sacrificer, the ancient Person, Virat, called Aniruddha, the origin and dissolution of the worlds.
When the night of Brahma had ended, by the grace of that one of boundless splendour, lotus-eyed one, a lotus appeared, and in it Brahma was born, born of his grace.
At the end of the day, from the forehead of the god, filled with anger, Rudra was born, the cause of destruction.
These two best of the gods, born of grace and anger, are remembered as the makers of creation and destruction on his command, mere instruments here, givers of boons to all beings.
The matted, the knotted, the shaven, frequenter of cremation grounds, bearer of fierce vows, Rudra the yogi, terrible to Tripura,
destroyer of Daksha's sacrifice and the taker of Bhaga's eyes, is to be known as Narayana's self, age after age, son of Pandu.
When Maheshvara, god of gods, is worshipped, the god Narayana, the lord, is also worshipped, Partha.
I am the self of all worlds, son of Pandu; therefore I worship Rudra, the self, first.
If I did not worship Ishana, the boon-giving Shiva, my mind thinks that no one would worship the self; I have made the standard, and the world follows.
Standards are to be honoured, therefore I worship him; he who knows him knows me, and he who follows him follows me.
Rudra and Narayana are one sattva made two; he moves in the world, standing in manifestation, in all actions, Kaunteya.
No boon is to be given to me by anyone, delight of the Pandavas; thinking so in mind, I worshipped the ancient lord of the universe for a son, the self by the self.
Vishnu does not bow to any god, except the self; therefore I worship Rudra.
The gods with Brahma, with Rudras, with Indra and the sages, worship the best of gods, the god Narayana Hari.
Of those who will be, those who are, and the beings, Bharata, Vishnu is the foremost of all, always to be served and worshipped.
Bow to Vishnu, giver of offerings, and to the giver of refuge; bow to the boon-giver, Kaunteya, bow to the enjoyer of offerings to gods and ancestors.
My devotees are of four kinds; this you have heard. Of them the single-minded are best, with no other deity; I alone am their goal, who act without desire.
The other three kinds of devotees are held to desire fruit; all are liable to fall; but the awakened one has the best share.
Those who serve Brahma, the dark-throated one, and the other deities that are remembered, the best of the awakened, have been told to you, Partha; this is the distinction concerning the devotee.
You and I, Kaunteya, are remembered as Nara and Narayana, entered into a human body for the lifting of the burden.
I know the yogas of the self, who I am and whence, Bharata; the dharma marked by withdrawal, and that of prosperity.
I alone am famed as the resort of men, the eternal; waters are called nara, the waters are the sons of Nara; they were my resting-place before, so I am Narayana.
I cover the whole world, becoming like the sun with its rays; I am the dwelling of all beings, so I am Vasudeva.
I am the goal of all beings and of creatures too, Bharata; heaven and earth are pervaded by me, Partha, and my splendour is greater.
I am the supervisor of beings at the end, and wishing that, Bharata; and by striding, Partha, I am called Vishnu.
Desiring success through self-control, people desire me; and I am in heaven, earth and the middle; so I am Damodara.
Prishni is said to be food, the Vedas, water and nectar; these are always in my womb; so I am Prishnigarbha.
The sages spoke of me thus when Trita was cast into the well: "Prishnigarbha, protect Trita"; one thus cast down was protected.
Then Trita, son of Brahma, the first and best of sages, rose from the well by reciting Prishnigarbha.
The rays which shine of the scorching sun, of fire and of the moon, are called my hair; therefore the all-knowing best of the twice-born call me Keshava.
The embryo laid in his wife by the great-souled Utathya... and when Utathya had vanished, once by the god's illusion, Brihaspati took his wife, Bharata.
Then, as that best of sages was in union, the embryo, endowed with the five elements, spoke, Kaunteya:
I came first, giver of boons; you should not trouble my mother. Hearing this, Brihaspati grew angry and cursed him:
Since you have forbidden me, going in union, therefore you will be born blind, by my curse; there is no doubt.
By the curse of that chief of sages he entered long darkness; he was the sage named Dirghatamas by name of old.
Having obtained the four eternal Vedas with their limbs and subsidiary limbs, he then employed this secret name of mine.
By rule in sequence, saying "Keshava" again and again, he became sighted and became Gautama again.
Thus, Arjuna, my name Keshava is a boon-giver to all the gods and great-souled sages.
Agni joined with Soma has been made one womb and mouth; therefore the whole universe, moving and unmoving, is of the nature of Agni and Soma.
It is also in the Purana: "Agni and Soma are of one womb and one nature, and the gods have Agni as their mouth"; and by being of one womb, honouring each other, they support the worlds.
[The Blessed One said:] Come, I shall tell you, son of Pandu, an old story, born of my own splendour, Partha; hear with one mind.

When the time of dissolution had passed, at the end of the fourth thousand ages, when the unmanifest and the dissolution of all beings had come, with moving and unmoving gone, devoid of light, earth and wind, in sinless darkness, in a world of one ocean of water, called only "darkness," in a second-less state, neither in night nor in day, neither being nor non-being, neither manifest nor unmanifest established: in this state, from Narayana, the refuge of qualities, imperishable, ageless, senseless, ungraspable, unborn, true, harmless, auspicious, of varied activities, imperishable, unageing and deathless, formless, all-pervading, maker of all, eternal darkness, the Person, Hari the unchanging, appeared.

There is also an illustration here: "There was not day nor night; there was not being nor non-being; darkness alone was before, of universal form; she is the mother of the universe": thus its meaning is explained.

At the appearance of Brahma, lotus-born, of that Person born of darkness, that Person, wishing to create creatures, created Agni and Soma from his eyes. Then, when the creation of beings proceeded, in the sequence of creatures came brahmanas and kshatriyas. What is Soma is Brahman; what is Brahman are brahmanas; what is Agni is kshatra; and from kshatra Brahman is stronger. Why? This is a quality evident to the world: no being higher than brahmanas was born before. He offers in the kindled fire; therefore I say: the creation of beings was made by Brahma, and the three worlds are held by establishing beings.

There is a mantra: "You, Agni, are the hotri of all sacrifices, placed by gods and men among all people"; and here is the illustration: "Agni, hotri of all sacrifices, placed by gods and men in the world"; for Agni is the hotri, maker of sacrifices, and that Agni is Brahman.

For without mantra there is no oblation, nor without the Person austerity; the offering and worship of the mantras are for gods and men; by this, "You are the hotri," he is appointed. And the offices of hotri that men hold belong to the brahmana; sacrificing for others is laid down not for kshatriyas and vaishyas, the twice-born. Therefore brahmanas, having become Agni, carry the sacrifices; sacrifices satisfy the gods; the gods nourish the earth.

In the Shatapatha Brahmana it is said: "He offers in the kindled fire who, being learned, offers a gift-oblation in a brahmana's mouth." So too learned brahmanas, become Agni, nourish Agni; Agni is Vishnu, who enters all beings and sustains their breaths. Here also there are verses sung by Sanatkumara:
Brahma first created the universe, the beginning of all, without remainder; by the sound of Brahman the immortals, whose womb is Brahman, stay in heaven.

The Vedas, Puranas and Itihasas are authorities, issued from Narayana's mouth; brahmanas are the self of all, makers of all, nourishers of all. For brahmanas first appeared together with the speech of that boon-giving god, and from brahmanas the other classes appeared. And thus brahmanas are distinguished among gods and asuras, when long ago I myself, having become Brahman, produced them; gods, asuras and great sages, distinct beings, were established and restrained.

For the sake of the violation of Ahalya, Indra got yellow-brown whiskers from Gautama; and for Kaushika's sake Indra lost his testicles and got a ram's. The arm of Purandara, who was raising his thunderbolt to prevent the Ashvins' share, was stiffened by Chyavana; and Daksha, angered by the slaying of the sacrifice, again joined himself to austerity, and another eye-form was made on Rudra's forehead.

Serpents appeared, sent against Rudra, who had undertaken the vow for the slaying of Tripura, by Ushanas, having uprooted a lock of his hair; pressed by those serpents, his throat was made blue; or in the earlier Svayambhuva interval, he got blue-throatedness from the grasp of Narayana's hand.

When Angiras Brihaspati, officiating in the churning for nectar, touched the waters, the waters did not become clear. Then Brihaspati was angry with the waters: "Since you became turbid when I touched you, from today be filled with fish, crocodiles, tortoises and creatures, and be turbid"; and from then the waters were filled with water-beasts.
Vishvarupa, son of Tvashtri, was the priest of the gods and the nephew of the asuras; he gave the share openly to the gods and secretly to the asuras.

Then the asuras, placing Hiranyakashipu in front, begged a boon from Vishvarupa's mother, his sister: "Sister, this son of yours, Tvashtra Vishvarupa of three heads, priest of the gods, gives the share openly to the gods and secretly to us. Thereby the gods increase and we decline; you ought to restrain him, so that he may serve us."

Then, when Vishvarupa had gone to Nandana grove, his mother said, "Son, why do you increase the other side and destroy your mother's kin? You should not do so." Thinking his mother's word not to be transgressed, Vishvarupa honoured Hiranyakashipu and went to him.

Hiranyakashipu received a curse from Vasishtha, born of Hiranyagarbha: "Because you chose another as hotri, your sacrifice will be unfinished, and you will get death from a being of a new kind"; and by that curse Hiranyakashipu got death.

Vishvarupa, increasing his mother's side, became exceedingly austere. To break his vow, Indra employed many beautiful apsarases; seeing them his mind was shaken, and he soon became attached to those apsarases. Knowing him attached, the apsarases said, "We shall go as we came."
Tvashtra's son said to them, "Where will you go? Stay with me for now; it will be well." They said to him, "God, we are women, apsarases; we chose long ago Indra, the mighty boon-giver."

Then Vishvarupa said, "Today the gods will be without Indra." He muttered mantras, and by those mantras the three-headed one grew; with one mouth he drank the Soma well offered by priests at sacrifices in all worlds, with another that of the gods with Indra. Then Indra, seeing him growing, all his limbs fed by the drinking of Soma, fell into worry.

The gods with Indra went to Brahma and said, "Vishvarupa drinks the Soma well offered in all sacrifices; we are left without a share. The asura side grows and we decline; you ought to ordain for us what is best hereafter."
Brahma said to them: "The sage Dadhicha of Bhrigu's line practises austerity; let him be asked for a boon, that he give up his body, and let a thunderbolt be made from his bones."

The gods went where the blessed sage Dadhicha practised austerity. The gods with Indra approached him and said, "Blessed one, is your austerity well and unobstructed?" Dadhicha said, "Welcome to you; what is to be done? I shall do what you say." They said to him, "The blessed one ought to give up his body for the good of the world." Then Dadhicha, unperturbed, equal in pleasure and pain, the great yogi, composing himself, gave up his body.

When he had gone to the Supreme Self, Dhatri took those bones and made a thunderbolt. With that thunderbolt, unbreakable and irresistible, born of the bones of a Brahman, entered by Vishnu, Indra killed Vishvarupa and cut off his heads. After that, Indra slew Vritra, the enemy produced by Tvashtri from the churning of Vishvarupa's body.

When that Vritra was split in two, in fear of the sin of killing a brahmana, Indra gave up the kingship of the gods and went to a cool lotus-pond born in the waters at Manasa lake; and there, by the power of lordship, becoming tiny, he entered a lotus-stalk.

Then, with the lord of the three worlds, the husband of Shachi, vanished from fear of the sin of killing a brahmana, the world became lordless, tamas and rajas entered the gods, the mantras did not work for the great sages, rakshasas appeared, Brahman went to destruction, and the worlds, without Indra, were weak and easily assailed.

Then the divine sages consecrated Nahusha, son of Ayu, as king of the gods; with five hundred flames on his forehead, taking away the splendour of all, Nahusha ruled heaven. Then the worlds regained their nature and became well.

Then Nahusha said, "Everything that Shakra enjoyed has come to me, except Shachi." So saying he went to Shachi and said to her, "Fair one, I am Indra of the gods; accept me." Shachi answered, "By nature you are fond of dharma and born in the lunar line; you should not violate another's wife."

Nahusha said to her, "The Indra office is held by me; I take the kingdom and jewel of Indra; there is no adharma in it; you were enjoyed by Indra." She said to him, "I have a vow not yet completed; at its conclusion I shall come to you in some days." Thus addressed by Shachi, Nahusha went away.

Then Shachi, afflicted with grief and sorrow, longing to see her husband, seized by fear of Nahusha, went to Brihaspati. Seeing her come, Brihaspati entered meditation, and knowing her intent on her husband's cause, said: "By this same vow and austerity, call the boon-giving goddess Upashruti; she will show you Indra."

She, established in the Great Observance, called the boon-giving goddess Upashruti with mantras. Upashruti came to Shachi and said, "Here I am, called by you; what dear thing shall I do for you?" Bowing her head, Shachi said, "Blessed one, you ought to show me my husband; you are held to be true." She led her to Manasa lake and showed Indra in the lotus-stalk.

Seeing his wife thin and weary, Indra thought: "Ah, a great sorrow has come to me today; she has come seeking me, lost, afflicted with sorrow." Indra said to her, "How do you manage?" She said, "Nahusha calls me, and I have set him a time."

Indra said to her: "Go; you must say to Nahusha: 'Come to me in a carriage unlike any before, yoked to sages, and carry it yourself; Indra's great vehicles, dear to the mind, have been ridden by me; you ought to come by another.'" Thus told, she went glad; Indra again entered the lotus-stalk.
Seeing Indrani come, Nahusha said, "That time is complete." Shachi spoke to him as Shakra had said. He mounted a vehicle drawn by great sages and came to Shachi.

Then Agastya, Maitravaruni, born of a jar, saw the great sages being driven by Nahusha and was touched by his foot. He said to Nahusha, "Doer of the forbidden, sinner, fall to the earth; become a serpent as long as earth and mountains stand." At the very moment of the great sage's word, he fell from that vehicle.

Then the three worlds were again without Indra, and the divine sages went to the blessed Vishnu for refuge for Indra's sake and said to him, "Blessed one, you ought to save Indra, overcome by the sin of killing a brahmana." Then the boon-giver said to them, "Let Shakra sacrifice with the horse sacrifice, the Vaishnava; then he will regain his own place."

Then, when the divine sages did not see Indra, they said to Shachi, "Go, fair one, bring Indra." She went again to that lake, and Indra rose from it and went to Brihaspati. Brihaspati brought the great horse sacrifice for Shakra; then, releasing a black-spotted horse fit for sacrifice and making that horse his mount, Brihaspati restored Indra, lord of the Maruts, to his own place.

Then that king of the gods, praised by gods and sages, in heaven became free of stain; he divided the sin of killing a brahmana into four places: women, fire, trees and cows. Thus Indra, strengthened by the power of brahmin splendour, having slain his enemy, was restored to his own place.

Once the great sage Bharadvaja, going to the sky-Ganga and touching the water, was met by Vishnu taking three strides; Bharadvaja struck his chest with a hand full of water, and he became marked on the chest.
Agni, cursed by the great sage Bhrigu, was made an eater of everything.

Aditi cooked food for the gods, "Having eaten this they will slay the asuras." There Budha came at the conclusion of her vow and begged alms from Aditi; she did not give. Angered by the refusal of alms, Budha, having become Brahman, in Vivasvan's second birth killed the egg of Aditi called Anda; he became Martanda, Vivasvan, god of offerings to ancestors.

Daksha had sixty daughters; of them he gave thirteen to Kashyapa, ten to Dharma, ten to Manu, and twenty-seven to Indu. Though they were equal and had the name of the lunar mansions, Soma showed extra love to Rohini. Then the others, the wives, jealous, went to their father and told this matter: "Blessed one, though we are equal in power, Soma serves Rohini more." He said, "Consumption will enter him."

By Daksha's curse, consumption entered Soma the king. Seized by consumption, he went to Daksha, and Daksha said, "You do not behave equally." The sages said to Soma, "You are wasting by consumption; in the western direction in the ocean is the sacred bathing-place Hiranyasaras; go there and bathe." Soma went to the tirtha Hiranyasaras and bathed himself, and freed himself of sin. Because Soma shone there, from then the tirtha became famous by the name Prabhasa. By that curse even now Soma wanes, standing at the new moon, and at the full moon shows his body covered by a line of cloud, taking a colour like a cloud; so his hare-mark became spotless.

The great sage Sthulashiras practised austerity in the north-east direction of Meru. As he practised austerity, a pure wind bearing every scent blew and touched his body. His body heated by austerity, lean, fanned by the wind, he reached heart's content. For him, so pleased by the fanning of the wind, the trees at once did not show the beauty of flowers; so he cursed them, "You will not be in flower at all times."

For the good of the world Narayana was long ago the great sage named Vadavamukha. When he practised austerity on Meru, the ocean called did not come; angered, by the heat of his own body he made the ocean's water still and gave it a saltness like sweat. And he said, "You will be undrinkable; and this water, drunk sweet by one named Vadavamukha, will become so"; even today the sea water is drunk by that one named Vadavamukha who follows.

Rudra desired Uma, daughter of the Himalaya mountain. The great sage Bhrigu also came to Himavat and said, "Give me your daughter Uma." Himavat said, "Rudra is the longed-for bridegroom." Bhrigu said to him, "Since you rejected me, who had made up my mind to ask for your daughter, you will not be a vessel of jewels." From then on that word of the sage stands.
Such is the greatness of brahmanas. Even kshatra, approaching the eternal, imperishable earth as wife, enjoyed her. This Brahman of Agni and Soma holds up the world.
By awakening and heating, the world is delighted; by these deeds done by Agni and Soma, son of Pandu, I am Hrishikesha, the lord, boon-giver, cherisher of the worlds.
By the yoga of this invocation, "Hare," I take my share at sacrifices; and my colour is the best of green; therefore I am remembered as Hari.
I am the essence of the worlds' abode, and truth has been reflected; therefore I am proclaimed by the brahmins as Ritadhama and as Satya.
Formerly I found the lost earth that had gone into a cave; the gods praised me with words as Govinda.
Shipivishta is a name, and one who is hairless; whatever is entered by him is called shipivishta.
The sage Yaska, unwavering, sang me in many sacrifices as Shipivishta; thus I bear a secret name.
Praising me as Shipivishta, the noble-minded sage Yaska, by my grace, obtained below the lost Nirukta.
I am not born, I am not born, and I never will be born; I am the knower of the field of all beings; therefore I am remembered as Aja.
I plough the earth, Partha, becoming the great black iron; since my colour is black, I am Krishna, Arjuna.
The earth was joined by me with water, the sky with wind, and the wind with fire; thus I am Vaikuntha.
Extinction is the highest happiness, and that is called supreme dharma; I have not fallen from it before, so by that deed I am Achyuta.
Earth and sky are both famed, worldly in the universe; to hold them both I am readily called Adhokshaja.
Those who know the Nirukta and those who think of the meaning of words sing me in the early lineage; it is established that I am Adhokshaja.
This was uttered by the great sages agreed in word; no other in the world is Adhokshaja except the lord Narayana.
Oghavan himself gave his daughter Oghavati to the learned Sudarshana, god-like in form, to be his wife.
Having formed the sacrifice in his mind, the grandson of Karandhama, eloquent, approached Brihaspati and spoke these words.
And this exertion was done exceedingly by you in begging me; from that, dear one, I became weary and as if senseless.
Thinking of the destruction of the Andhakas and Vrishnis and the end of the Kurus, that greatly mighty one then judged it the time for his departure, and restrained his senses.
Hell must be seen by all kings, dear one; so you have gained this moment of the highest sorrow.
